spot.html_text: The commitment to the scientific approach had become so deeply embedded in the thinking of the time that providing a theory open to confirmation or refutation through observation and the provision of evidence to support one’s claims was taken to be the hallmark of sound argument. This is particularly apparent in the work of Adam Ferguson (1723–1816).
